newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QMC shares sizzle on magnesium deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QMC shares sizzle on magnesium deal.

text.p: Shares in metals processor, Queensland Metals Corporation Ltd (QMC), soared nearly 30 percent to a 2-1/2 year high of A$1.51 in morning trade on Thursday after it announced development of the Magmetal magnesium project in Queensland.
Normandy and QMC said in a joint announcement that they would develop the QMC magnesium metals project (Magmetal), with each group holding 50 percent of the project.

The companies said Ford Motor Co and the government-owned Commonwealth Scientific Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) are to financially contribute to the Magmetal development as non-equity partners, along with marketing and technical input.

It said as part of a pre-commercial phase, a 1,000 tonnes per annum pilot plant which converts magnesite to magnesium metal is to be constructed and a full feasibility study completed. This is estimated to cost A$73 million, it said.
If it goes ahead the project is expected about A$700 million to develop and would produce about 90,000 tonnes.
"It's drifting back from that A$1.50 level but it looks a good deal for the company," said a Brisbane dealer.
By 12.30 p.m. (0130 GMT), QMC shares had eased to be up 17 cents on the day at A$1.34 on turnover of 1.3 million shares.
Normandy shares were two cents up at A$1.60 on turnover of 1.6 million shares.
